subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` fields be allowed to override later stricter global or agent exec security config after a Discord session resumes?
rationale: Current source, tests, and docs make persisted session defaults intentional, but the reported failure mode is security-sensitive because later operator policy changes can be shadowed by old session state.

options.title: Make global policy an upper bound
options.body: Clamp or clear stored session exec fields that exceed current global or agent exec security policy, with migration/reset coverage for existing sessions.

options.title: Keep session persistence as-is
options.body: Document that operators must reset sessions or use a repair flow to enforce changed exec policy for existing lanes.

options.title: Add explicit reset first
options.body: Ship an operator-facing session exec reset or doctor repair before changing precedence semantics for existing sessions.

recommendation.title: Make global policy an upper bound
recommendation.body: Clamp or clear stored session exec fields that exceed current global or agent exec security policy, with migration/reset coverage for existing sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail for the `/exec` session override behavior and focused tests points to steipete, and this is a product/security policy decision around that behavior.
